story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Think of it this way: Autonomic networking follows the concept of Autonomic Computing, an initiative started by IBM in 2001. And here is the clever part: Its ultimate aim is to create self-managing networks to overcome the rapidly growing complexity of the Internet and other networks and to enable their further growth, far beyond the size of today. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. And that shape of the machine — Autonomic networking — is what makes everything else possible.
